Subject: Private VPC deployment — initial asks and constraints

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Greenline is ready to move to an air-gapped private deployment for PHI workloads. Before we lock dates with our colo partner we wanted a short architecture review with Redwood to validate assumptions. Top-level constraints:

- Air-gapped (no direct internet egress from inference nodes). Any external telemetry must traverse our audited egress proxy in the DMZ.
- Physical cross-connect to our Oregon colo (Equiv): 1 x 10Gb, no BGP peering with Redwood-managed routers (we cannot exchange routes).
- Per-tenant KV cache isolation (customer has strict data-segmentation policy).
- Nodes will be high-density inference (32GB A100 equivalent), expect bursts up to 600 qps across the cluster.
- SOC 2 evidence required for the control plane connectivity path and audit logs.

Can your team review a proposed reference diagram and call out any blockers (especially around egress proofing, KV cache topology, and acceptance criteria for canary)? Attaching our initial checklist (simple template).

Thanks,
Samira

Director, Cloud Ops — Greenline Health

Adding a few notes ahead of Tuesday

Short summary of proposed reference architecture (attached drawing):
- Control plane placement: terminate customer-to-Redwood control-plane link over a customer-initiated TLS tunnel to a dedicated control-plane endpoint in the Oregon private region. No east-west routing from Redwood into customer network; control-plane is API-only (pull/push model).
- Data plane (inference): lives entirely in customer colo behind the cross-connect. We recommend colocating inference clusters inside the tenant VLAN and using a sidecar proxy pattern for egress.
- Egress: all telemetry/metrics/traces must exit via customer DMZ proxy. We will support a mutually-agreed TLS egress channel to that proxy; Redwood agents will only communicate outbound to the proxy IPs you provide.
- KV cache isolation: use per-tenant namespaces + process-level isolation. Where latency budget is tight, provision a local read-replica per rack. Avoid a shared global Redis unless you are comfortable with layered encryption and strict ACLs.
- Autoscaling: prefer node-based scale-up with target latency SLO (p90) and a burst buffer that uses queued requests redirected to dedicated burst pool.

Open questions / risks:
1) The no-BGP constraint means we cannot advertise any service IPs into customer fabric — we need either: cross-connected VIPs that customer routes locally, or an L3 proxy in the DMZ.
2) SOC2 evidence: we can provide control-plane audit logs and signed acceptance runbook but will need explicit sign-off on the telemetry egress path (customer must allow outbound TLS to the proxy endpoints).
3) KV cache warmup strategy for canary: recommend a warmup window where we pre-populate hot keys from a snapshot (ops script) and run synthetic load to validate correctness.

Attaching: glh_vpc_reference_v1.drawio (diagram), and a short deployment checklist snippet. We'll refine on the call.

-Marissa

Quick ops-oriented items to discuss on Tuesday:

- KV cache topology: per-tenant namespace + per-rack replica. If Greenline expects <8ms p95 on KV hits, we should place replicas in the same rack. Otherwise, measure impact of cross-rack reads under peak.
- Networking: because no BGP, we will need either a static route map for VIPs on the customer edge or NAT from the DMZ proxy. Static routes are preferred for predictability.
- Ports/ACLs: control-plane TLS (443) outbound to our control endpoint; egress proxy port (3129 or 443) depending on their proxy. We should provide a minimal port list: 443, 10250 (kube-probes), 9090 (metrics) — all outbound to specific proxy IPs.
- Canary plan:
  * Phase 0: dry-run in a mirror VLAN with synthetic traffic.
  * Phase 1: 5% traffic to canary pool with KV warmup.
  * Phase 2: 25% increase, monitor token-cost/regression.
  * Phase 3: full cutover with rollback tags.
- Observability: require a pull model for logs (Greenline pulls audit bundles from our signed S3 endpoint) since inbound fetches are blocked. Need retention window (suggest 90 days) and signed digests for tamper-proofing.

I attached a concise ops checklist to iterate on during the call. Also flagged a minor compatibility concern: quantized model builds for A100-32G can degrade warm-start times — advise we test a 30-minute warmup window in canary.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
